comments.body:
Fix pushed for review: Gerrit change 2558 — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2558 (commit 437d8790c632, branch reb-febd-uv-pin, 5 files +235/-4).

## The diagnosis was reproduced locally, not merely inferred

Building `Dockerfile.opcert` with `:latest` and `--no-cache` reproduced the production failure verbatim: `error: Required uv version ==0.12.7 does not match the running version 0.12.9`, exit code 2. After the fix the same build exits 0, resolves `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.7@sha256:95f2aa1f...`, completes `uv sync --locked`, and `docker run --entrypoint uv` reports `uv 0.12.7 (aarch64-unknown-linux-musl)`. Only opcert was built (smallest); mcp and reviewbot carry the identical COPY line and the identical fix.

## AC3 gate written FIRST and seen RED

    FAILED test_real_repository_dockerfiles_do_not_float_the_uv_tag
      AssertionError: floating :latest toolchain tags: [
        'infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:90',
        'infra/compose/Dockerfile.opcert:37',
        'infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:112']
    FAILED test_real_repository_dockerfiles_match_the_pyproject_pin
    FAILED test_dockerfile_floating_uv_tag_is_rejected
    FAILED test_dockerfile_uv_tag_skewed_from_pyproject_is_rejected
    FAILED test_dockerfile_untagged_uv_reference_is_rejected
    FAILED test_dockerfile_floating_base_image_is_rejected
    6 failed, 20 passed

All three offenders flagged, and the four fixture tests confirm the gate previously had NO Dockerfile coverage at all.

## AC2 — no new mechanism was added

`scripts/check_uv_pin.py` already existed, already parses `[tool.uv] required-version` from pyproject.toml, exists for exactly this defect class on the CI side, and is already wired into `make lint`. It was EXTENDED rather than duplicated. It now fails on a uv tag differing from required-version (naming both versions), on any floating `:latest`, and on an omitted tag (an omitted tag IS `:latest`), while allowing named build stages, stage indices, and `@sha256:` digest pins. `make lint`'s mechanism-delta ratchet confirms new=0.

Rejected alternatives, recorded so this is not relitigated:
- **ARG UV_VERSION from compose** — the compose build blocks have no `args:` today, so it needs new plumbing AND autodeploy.sh must preserve it; worse, a plain `docker build -f Dockerfile.mcp .` falls back to the ARG default, so the literal still lives in each Dockerfile plus a second copy in compose. Strictly more places to drift.
- **A new .github/uv-version.txt** (mirroring module-size-limit.txt) — pyproject's required-version is ALREADY the single source; uv reads it directly and it is what actually fails the build. A second file makes two sources of truth needing their own equality gate — the same problem one level up. The module-size-limit.txt precedent applies where no canonical declaration exists; here one does.
- **Bumping required-version to 0.12.9** — rejected per AC; it fixes nothing, because the images would still float and break at the next upstream release.

## Blast radius — full sweep

Fixed: the three uv lines. Already clean: every other image reference — python:3.12-slim (x3), gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1, and tests/external/live_jira_dc/Dockerfile (digest-pinned).

Correctly NOT flagged: `:latest` in autodeploy.sh and the runbooks refers to LOCAL image tags (compose-review-bot:latest, $MCP_IMAGE:latest) used for the :prev/:latest rollback dance. Locally produced, cannot float; a `_is_registry_reference` split keeps them out.

ONE ITEM LEFT DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE, needing a decision: `docker-compose.langfuse.yml:113` runs `image: docker.io/minio/minio:latest`. Same defect class, but it is a compose `image:` key rather than a Dockerfile, so AC3 as written does not cover it, and choosing a MinIO version could not be validated here. Lower blast radius (dev/observability stack, no build gate depends on it). Widening the gate to compose `image:` keys is a small follow-up if wanted.

## Verification

test_uv_pin_guard.py 26 passed; `-k "docker or uv or pin or image"` 601 passed / 6 skipped; MCP + opcert infra suites 76 passed; make lint exit 0; make typecheck Success across 744 files; verify-commit-ticket OK.

## Recovery note

Landing this does not by itself clear the 502. It restores the ability to BUILD; the MCP container is separately dead (OOM, bug 9ea3), so the endpoint recovers only once autodeploy completes a successful rebuild and cutover. AC4 (deployed-sha advancing to current origin/main) is the confirmation to watch.

compiled_state.description:
## Observed — ONGOING PRODUCTION OUTAGE

Every `docker compose build` on the rebar-gerrit host fails at the `uv sync` layer:

    #16 [mcp stage-0 7/8] RUN uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra mcp --extra bedrock
    #16 0.304 error: Required uv version `==0.12.7` does not match the running version `0.12.9`
    failed to solve: ... exit code: 2

Captured from `journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy` on i-00880b2c7f13527c5 at 2026-09-03 05:02 and 05:06 UTC. The failure repeats every autodeploy tick, escalating the backoff (fail#3 240s, fail#4 480s), and `rebar-autodeploy.service` reports 'Failed with result exit-code' each time.

## Root cause — an exact pin against a floating tag

`pyproject.toml:346` declares `required-version = "==0.12.7"`, added by commit `7501cc1d602d` ('Pin uv once so CI stops resolving it remotely'). uv reads `required-version` itself and fails fast when the running binary differs.

But the container builds do NOT install a pinned uv. All three copy from a FLOATING tag:

- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:90`
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:112`
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.opcert:37`

each `COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest /uv /usr/local/bin/uv`.

`:latest` has since moved to 0.12.9, so the pin and the binary disagree and every build dies. The CI path was fixed by the same pin commit via `.github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml`, which DOES pin a version — the three Dockerfiles were left behind. This is a time bomb by construction: it fires whenever upstream publishes, with no change to this repo.

## Blast radius — wider than it currently looks

MCP is the only VISIBLY broken service because its container is separately dead (OOM-killed, see `9ea3-7d07-ea55-4496`) and therefore needs a rebuild it can never complete. The review-bot and opcert containers are still serving their last-known-good images, so they LOOK healthy — but their builds are equally broken, and any restart, host reboot, or deploy touching them turns this into a second outage. The box is currently not tracking main at all.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: container builds no longer resolve uv from a floating tag. All three Dockerfiles pull a uv whose version satisfies `required-version` in pyproject.toml. Verified by a successful `docker compose build` of each.
- [ ] AC2: the pinned uv version is SINGLE-SOURCED, not copied into four places. A drift between `pyproject.toml`'s `required-version` and what the images install must be impossible-by-construction or caught by a gate, not left to review. Verified by changing the pin and observing the gate or build fail.
- [ ] AC3: a test or CI gate fails when any Dockerfile references a floating `:latest` tag for a version-sensitive toolchain image. Verified by adding `:latest` back to one Dockerfile and seeing it fail.
- [ ] AC4 [non-codebase]: the box is confirmed tracking main again — `rebar-autodeploy` completes a deploy and `deployed-sha` advances to current origin/main.

## Testing

- `docker compose -f infra/compose/docker-compose.yml build mcp reviewbot opcert`
- the AC3 gate test
- post-fix: `journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy` shows a clean cutover
